title: Find the Best Continuous Recommendation Window
real_world_story: A recommendation system receives a sequence of item scores representing items shown during a user's browsing session. The system wants to identify a continuous group of K items with the highest total recommendation score.

real_world_connection.input_represents: Scores of items in the order they were displayed
real_world_connection.target_represents: Number of consecutive items to consider
real_world_connection.algorithm_represents: A sliding window that maintains the sum of the current K-item section efficiently

problem_statement: Given an array of item scores and an integer K, find the maximum sum of any contiguous subarray of exactly K elements.
task: Find the continuous group of K items having the maximum total recommendation score.
input_format: The first line contains an integer N. The second line contains N space-separated integers representing item scores. The third line contains K.
output_format: Print the maximum sum of any contiguous group of exactly K item scores.

examples.explanation: The window 8, 2, 9 has the maximum sum of 19.
The windows have sums 6, 9, 8, and 7, so the maximum is 9.

expected_algorithm.name: Sliding Window
expected_algorithm.reason: A sliding window avoids recomputing the sum of every K-element section from scratch.

hint: Calculate the sum of the first K items.
Move the window one position at a time.
Subtract the score leaving the window.
Add the new score entering the window and update the maximum.
real_world_takeaway: Sliding Window techniques help recommendation systems analyze continuous browsing or interaction segments efficiently.
